mainTopic: How ארץ ישראל was divided (by יוצאי מצרים, by באי הארץ, or by both), and רב פפא's questions to אביי on this
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that brings two פסוקים together. It says ארץ ישראל was split according to both groups: those who left מצרים (יוצאי מצרים) and those who entered the land (באי הארץ). Someone who belonged to both groups took a share from each. The ברייתא then explains what happened to the portions of the sinners in the desert. יהושע and כלב took the portions of the מרגלים. The מתלוננים and עדת קרח lost their own share, but their sons inherited through their grandfathers. The גמרא asks how we know the פסוק 'לשמות מטות אבותם' is about יוצאי מצרים and not just the שבטים. It answers from 'ונתתי אתה לכם מורשה', which was said to the generation that left מצרים. A סימן then lists a series of questions רב פפא asked אביי. The first one begins here: the פסוק 'לרב תרבה נחלתו' fits the view that the land was divided by יוצאי מצרים. His challenge to the other view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The land was divided by both groups
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that ארץ ישראל was divided according to both יוצאי מצרים and באי הארץ, so that both פסוקים are kept. It then explains how that works in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The land was divided for both groups, so that both verses are fulfilled. How? If a person left Egypt, he takes a share with those who left Egypt. If he entered the land, he takes a share with those who entered. If he was in both groups, he takes a share from both.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a middle opinion: the land was divided by both groups, not just one. It then spells out the three possible cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק points to the fathers (יוצאי מצרים) and another points to the people actually entering (באי הארץ). Instead of choosing one פסוק, this view keeps both. As a result, a person who both left מצרים and entered the land gets a double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who left Egypt (the generation of the Exodus)
Those who entered the land (the generation that came into ארץ ישראל)
The land was divided
How so? (a phrase that opens an explanation)
He takes his share

steps.confusionAlert: 'מכאן ומכאן' does not mean he chooses which group to take from. It means he gets two shares, one with each group.

phrases.english: The land was divided to these and to those,
phrases.notes: 'These and those' means יוצאי מצרים and באי הארץ, the two groups from the two פסוקים.

phrases.english: in order to uphold these two verses.
How so?
If he was from those who left Egypt,
he takes his share with those who left Egypt.
If he was from those who entered the land,
he takes his share with those who entered the land.
If he was from here and from there,
he takes his share from here and from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section, giving a view that combines both פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The land was divided by both יוצאי מצרים and באי הארץ. Someone in both groups receives two shares.

steps.title: The portions of the מרגלים, the מתלוננים and עדת קרח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. יהושע and כלב took the portions of the מרגלים. The מתלוננים and עדת קרח got no share themselves, but their sons inherited through their grandfathers.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for the מרגלים, יהושע and כלב took their portions. The מתלוננים and עדת קרח had no share in the land, but their sons took shares in the merit of their fathers' fathers and their mothers' fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what happened to the shares of people who sinned in the desert. The spies' portions went to יהושע and כלב. The מתלוננים and עדת קרח lost their own share, but their sons still inherited through their grandfathers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten מרגלים lost their portions, and the two loyal מרגלים, יהושע and כלב, received them. The מתלוננים and עדת קרח lost their own share. Their children still inherited through their grandfathers, on both the father's side and the mother's side.

keyTerms.meaning: The spies sent to scout the land
The complainers in the desert
Korah's group, who rebelled against משה
In the merit of / by right of
Their mothers' fathers (their maternal grandfathers)

phrases.english: The spies:
Joshua and Caleb took their portion.
phrases.notes: 'Their portion' means the share of the ten spies; יהושע and כלב got what the spies lost.

phrases.english: The complainers and the assembly of Korah:
they had no share in the land;
the sons took in the merit of their fathers' fathers,
and in the merit of their mothers' fathers.

steps.whatToRemember: The land was shared by both generations. The sins of the desert removed the sinners' own portions, but not their children's inheritance through grandfathers.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds special cases to the general rule of dividing the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע and כלב received the portions of the מרגלים. The מתלוננים and עדת קרח lost their own share, but their sons inherited through their grandfathers.

steps.title: Is the verse really about those who left Egypt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that 'לשמות מטות אבותם' refers to יוצאי מצרים. Maybe it refers to the original שבטים, meaning the land is simply divided into twelve tribal parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this verse, 'according to the names of the tribes of their fathers', is written about those who left Egypt? Maybe it is talking about the tribes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges a basic assumption of the ברייתא: that 'their fathers' means the people who left מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אבותם' means the founders of the twelve שבטים, the פסוק only tells us the land goes to twelve tribes. It would then say nothing about the generation of יוצאי מצרים. That would remove the source for giving that generation a share.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows / how do we know
According to the names of the tribes of their fathers
Perhaps / maybe
The tribes (or the tribal founders)

phrases.english: What shows that this verse,
'According to the names of the tribes of their fathers',
is written about those who left Egypt?
Perhaps it is said about the tribes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the ברייתא reads one of its two פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אבותם' in the פסוק means יוצאי מצרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'fathers' could just mean the founders of the twelve שבטים. In that case the פסוק gives no share to the Exodus generation.

steps.title: Proof from 'I will give it to you as an inheritance'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the פסוק 'ונתתי אתה לכם מורשה'. It describes the land as an inheritance from the fathers, and it was said to יוצאי מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And I will give it to you as a heritage, I am ה׳.' This means it is an inheritance for you from your fathers, and this was said to those who left Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different פסוק to show that 'fathers' means the generation that left מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מורשה' shows that the land comes as an inheritance from fathers. Since this פסוק was told to the generation that left מצרים, they are the 'fathers' the land is inherited from. This supports reading 'לשמות מטות אבותם' as being about יוצאי מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: A heritage / inheritance
Inheritance passed down from parents
From your fathers

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And I will give it to you as a heritage, I am ה׳' —
it is an inheritance for you from your fathers;
and He said it to those who left Egypt.
phrases.notes: This פסוק is part of what ה׳ told משה to say to the Jews in מצרים, before they left.

steps.whatToRemember: The source that יוצאי מצרים have a share is 'מורשה', which means inheritance from fathers and was spoken to the Exodus generation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a supporting פסוק that defines who the 'fathers' are.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Their fathers' might just mean the founders of the שבטים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The land is an inheritance from fathers, and that was said to יוצאי מצרים. So they are the fathers meant by the פסוק.

steps.title: A memory aid for the questions coming next
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a list of key words, to help remember a series of questions about dividing the land that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: To the more; צלפחד; and יוסף; contested; מנשה; will count.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. The גמרא is setting up the next section by giving a list of code words, one for each question that is about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one question in the upcoming series about how the land was divided. Examples are words about צלפחד, יוסף and מנשה. The list helps a learner keep the questions in order.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid / list of key words
צלפחד, whose daughters claimed his share in the land
Was contested / was argued over
Will count / will be reckoned

phrases.english: (Memory aid: To the more; Zelophehad;
and Joseph; contested;
Manasseh; will count.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition that prepares the next series of questions about dividing the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; this is a list of key words for the questions that follow.

steps.title: רב פפא begins his question: the פסוק fits the יוצאי מצרים view
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא tells אביי that the view saying the land was divided according to יוצאי מצרים fits the פסוק 'לרב תרבה נחלתו ולמעט תמעיט נחלתו'. He is setting up a difficulty for the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: It makes sense according to the one who says the land was divided according to those who left מצרים. That is what the פסוק means: 'To the many you shall give a bigger inheritance, and to the few you shall give a smaller inheritance.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts the first question from the סימן by saying which view fits a פסוק well. This is a setup line. The real challenge, against the other view, comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בשלמא sentence has two halves: 'This view works well...' and then 'but according to the other view, there is a problem.' Here we only hear the first half. The פסוק about giving more land to the many fits the view that the land was divided according to יוצאי מצרים. Soon רב פפא will ask how the פסוק fits the view that it was divided according to באי הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted' or 'it makes sense.' It opens a two-part question: one view fits well, but the other view has a problem.
According to the one who says.
The land was divided.
'This is what is written.' It shows that a פסוק fits well with a certain view.
'To the many you shall give a bigger inheritance.' A larger group gets a larger share of land.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at the end of this line and think the question is over. A בשלמא only says what works. The real problem, for the באי הארץ view, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Granted, according to the one who says
that the land was divided according to those who left Egypt,
this is what is written:
"To the many you shall give more inheritance,
and to the few you shall give less inheritance."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first question promised by the סימן in step 5. It returns to the dispute behind the ברייתא of whether the land was divided by יוצאי מצרים or by באי הארץ. Step 1 gave the middle view that combines both.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the land was divided according to באי הארץ. This line only sets up the attack by showing that the יוצאי מצרים view fits the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'לרב תרבה נחלתו' fits the יוצאי מצרים view. The unstated implication, spelled out next, is that the באי הארץ view has trouble explaining this פסוק.
